# Kaku: an AI-friendly Mac terminal

> Kaku is an AI-friendly Mac terminal with sensible defaults, ready out of the box. It is open source (MIT), needs no account, and connects to the AI service you configure yourself. This file is a complete, citable summary for language models and answer engines.

Homepage: https://kaku.fun
Source: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku
Author: Tw93 (also created Pake and Mole)
Latest version: 0.20.0
Platform: macOS only (Windows and Linux are not supported yet)
License: MIT

## What Kaku is

Kaku is a macOS-native terminal emulator derived from WezTerm and tuned for AI-assisted terminal work. It keeps the speed and Lua configurability of WezTerm but trims the binary and ships opinionated defaults so it is useful the moment it is installed. The goal is a terminal that lets you start working first, instead of configuring for an afternoon.

Kaku uses WezTerm's Lua configuration system. Some upstream features differ; review the Kaku configuration guide when reusing a config. AI is optional and uses the service you configure yourself. Kaku does not provide or relay AI services.

## Installation

- Download the DMG from GitHub Releases: https://github.com/tw93/Kaku/releases/latest
- Or install with Homebrew: `brew install tw93/tap/kakuku`
  - The tap formula is named `kakuku` because an unrelated `kaku` package already exists in Homebrew; the tap path avoids installing the wrong one.
- After installing, run `kaku doctor` to verify the app, PATH, and shell integration.

## Core features

- Mouse actions: right-click inside a pane to paste, search, open AI chat or the command palette, split, or close that pane. Cmd+Click opens URLs and file paths, keeping automatically wrapped URLs intact.
- Tabs and panes: new tab (Cmd+T), close (Cmd+W), switch (Cmd+1 to Cmd+9), find any tab or pane with Tab Navigator (Cmd+Shift+O), split panes (Cmd+D and Cmd+Shift+D), and navigate panes (Cmd+Option+arrows). Reopening Kaku restores windows, panes, and each pane's directory. Pane input broadcast was removed in v0.19.0 for safety; its old key assignments now do nothing.
- Preset defaults: JetBrains Mono, macOS-quality font rendering, and automatic dark and light themes that follow the system.
- Rendering: GPU-accelerated terminal text and graphics.
- Built-in AI assistant: when a command fails, Kaku drafts a fix for review. Press Cmd+Shift+E to paste the suggestion at the prompt; nothing runs on its own. Type `#` followed by a sentence to turn plain language into a command. Press Cmd+L to open AI chat once the assistant is configured.
- Curated shell suite: Lazygit (Cmd+Shift+G), Yazi file manager (Cmd+Shift+Y), remote files (Cmd+Shift+R), plus z, completion, and syntax highlighting preconfigured.
- Remote sessions: ssh, mosh, autossh, and et panes are labelled with the host name instead of a local path. In a remote pane AI chat disables local file and shell tools, because the working directory lives on the other host, and suggests commands to run there instead. Panes opened through an ssh domain return to their remote directory when a session is restored.
- Small touches: copy on select, clickable file paths, history peek, and a visual bell.
- Lua config: customize the terminal with WezTerm's Lua configuration system.

## AI setup

Run `kaku ai` to enable Kaku Assistant, choose Auth Type (`codex` to reuse a Codex login, or `api_key` for OpenAI-compatible endpoints), then set Simple Model and Deep Model. For custom endpoints, keep Auth Type set to API key and fill Base URL, API key, and model names manually. Once configured, Cmd+L opens the chat overlay. You configure your own AI service. Kaku does not provide or relay it.

## Command line

- `kaku doctor`: verify the app bundle, PATH, and shell integration, with fixes suggested for common problems.
- `kaku ai`: configure Kaku Assistant auth, models, Base URL, and API key.
- `kaku config`: adjust font size, opacity, Smart Tab, close confirmation, shortcuts, and Lua overrides from a TUI.
- `kaku update`: update the app in place. On macOS it verifies the package checksum and code signature before replacing the installed app.

## How Kaku compares

- vs iTerm2: Kaku includes preset fonts, themes, shell integration, and Mac shortcuts, with an optional assistant connected to your own AI service.
- vs Warp: Kaku is MIT licensed and requires no Kaku account. You configure your own AI service, and can customize the terminal with Lua.
- vs WezTerm: Kaku is based on WezTerm's engine and Lua configuration system, with Mac defaults, shell integration, and an optional AI assistant.

## Frequently asked questions

- How do I install Kaku? Download the DMG from GitHub Releases, or use the Homebrew tap: `brew install tw93/tap/kakuku`.
- Is Kaku paid? No. Kaku is an MIT-licensed open source project.
- Does Kaku run on Windows or Linux? Not yet. The current focus is making the native macOS experience solid first.
- Do I need a Kaku account? No. Configure your own AI service through `kaku ai`.
- Can I reuse my WezTerm config? Yes. Kaku uses WezTerm's Lua configuration system; some upstream behavior differs.
